amends: bench-v1.2 (configs/benchmark_protocol_v1.2_families.json and frozen/benchmark_protocol_v1.2.sha256, both kept unchanged) and through it bench-v1.1 (configs/benchmark_protocol_v1.json, unchanged): no metric definition or parameter, no family and no paper suite changes; the v1.1 metric-level tables are unchanged
status: pre-registered in frozen/benchmark_protocol_v1.2.1.sha256 before any protocol metric was computed on an evaluation dataset (scripts/eval_bench.py refused every evaluation dataset from bench-v1.2 until this freeze). NOT blind to the tuning city: see 'disclosure'.

disclosure.v1.2: When bench-v1.2 (family headline) was ordered and written on 2026-10-21, the Jakarta bench-v1.1 result was known to the project: TrajPE v3 vs DP-LoRA v2 (vp, 0.5B) won 34 and lost 54 of 88 primary metric cells, losing mainly on travel distance/length (counted 5 times), diameter (4 times), cell transitions, frequent pattern F1 and destination, and DP-LoRA v2 7B ranked significantly better (Nemenyi). The amendment was motivated by the protocol review's near-duplicate finding, but grouping these repeated metrics reduces the weight of exactly the metrics TrajPE v3 lost on Jakarta. Its writer did not open result files; the coordinator who ordered it knew the pattern.
disclosure.v1.2.1: When bench-v1.2.1 was written on 2026-10-22, the Jakarta bench-v1.2 family result of TrajPE v3.2 (candidate E2, 3 seeds) was known: vs DP-LoRA v2 7B 26 family wins, 0 ties, 22 losses, not significant, average family rank 1.86 (E2) vs 1.80 (7B); vs DP-LoRA v2 vp 0.5B a significant win (Holm p = 0.04). Also known: bench-v1.1 metric level, E2 won 50 of 88 cells against both DP-LoRA v2 vp and 7B, 33/44 at eps 4 and 17/44 at eps 1. The change of the family score D (rule 'metric_difference') was specified by the review of bench-v1.2 from the definition of d (higher-is-better metrics with values far below 1, e.g. next-POI acc/MRR, were shrunk about 10x by the 1 - v loss), not from results; its effect on the Jakarta comparison was not computed before this freeze. TrajPE v3.2's Markov next-POI MRR on Jakarta was known to be on par with or slightly above DP-LoRA v2's, so the change is expected to increase the weight of a family where TrajPE is not behind.
disclosure.consequence: Because neither amendment is blind to the tuning city, the bench-v1.1 metric-level headline and per-paper counts are reported with the same prominence as the bench-v1.2.1 family headline and per-paper verdicts (rule 'reporting'); a claim must hold under both or state where they differ.

purpose: bench-v1.2.1 fixes the three major findings of the bench-v1.2 review before any evaluation dataset is scored: (1) the family score D now averages a metric difference on each metric's natural scale for both directions, (2) the amendments' knowledge of the Jakarta results is disclosed and the v1.1 headline is reported with equal prominence, (3) scripts/eval_bench.py checks this freeze. It also states the tests under the owner's seed-0-only rule (2026-10-22) and adds the feature descriptors of the v3.2 workload families to the v3 split. The v1.1 headline counts every primary metric as an independent cell, but several primary metrics compare the same statistic of the same data with a different binning, grid, divergence or query set (travel distance x5, diameter x4, Kendall tau x3, pattern support x4, ...). bench-v1.2 groups the primary metrics into statistic families, counts each family once per dataset x epsilon, and adds a verdict per source paper on that paper's own metrics. The v1.1 metric-level tables are still reported unchanged; the v1.2 family-level headline is the primary headline from bench-v1.2 on.
changes_from_v1.2: statistics.metric_difference: d = s (v_ours - v_base) / (|v_ours| + |v_base|) (s = +1 higher-is-better, -1 lower-is-better) replaces the v1.1 loss-scale d inside the family score; v1.1 tables keep the v1.1 d
statistics.seeds and statistics.per_cell: one release per method x dataset x eps (seed 0); no per-cell test; paired tests across cells
reporting: v1.1 metric-level headline with equal prominence; disclosure
v3_split_descriptors: tdist, diam, od6, ctrans6, tcell6

family_rule.same_family: two primary metrics belong to one family when they compare the same empirical distribution (same unit of observation and same variables) with the same kind of comparison
family_rule.ignored: resolution (grid size, cell vs venue, number of bins or buckets, bucket range), divergence (JSD variant, smoothing), squared vs plain distance, joint vs start-conditional form of the same pair of variables, query shape and number, top-k size and pattern lengths, tie conventions, counting a pattern by occurrences or by trajectories that contain it, and time-of-day vs time-of-week resolution
family_rule.units: check-in point; hop (consecutive check-in pair); trail; trail coverage (trail x region incidence); pattern (contiguous cell sub-sequence); time-located point
family_rule.time_split: a metric whose statistic includes a time variable (timestamp window, time of day/week) is not in the same family as its time-free counterpart
family_rule.next_poi: one family per downstream model (transformer, markov): its 7 primary metrics (acc@1, acc@5, acc@10, acc@20, ndcg@5, ndcg@10, mrr, scope last) are rankings of the same predictions
family_rule.excluded: variants (movesim_grank_rank, movesim_irank_rank, llmob_si_code, llmob_dard_code, llmob_stvd_code), duplicates (ldp_trip_error, retra_trip_error), next-POI scope 'all' and next-POI models that are not registered in the protocol are reported in the v1.1 tables only

step_distance.variables: distance between consecutive locations (MoveSim squares it)

origin_destination.kind: distribution divergence (AdaTrace joint, HRNet conditional on the 30 most frequent starts)

step_interval.variables: time between consecutive check-ins (MoveSim merges consecutive check-ins at one venue into a stay)

venue_popularity.variables: visit probabilities of the most visited venues

nextpoi_transformer.variables: next-POI predictions of the transformer trained on the release

nextpoi_markov.variables: next-POI predictions of the Markov model trained on the release

paper_suites.rule: a paper's suite is the primary metrics whose source_paper is that paper (configs/benchmark_protocol_v1.json); next-POI belongs to Massive-STEPS; the code checks that this list equals the source_paper field

statistics.metric_difference: per (dataset, eps, primary metric) and baseline, on the seed-0 values v_ours and v_base: d = (v_ours - v_base) / (|v_ours| + |v_base|) for higher-is-better metrics and d = (v_base - v_ours) / (|v_base| + |v_ours|) for lower-is-better metrics; d = 0 when both are 0. d is in [-1, 1], scale-free on the metric's natural scale, symmetric in the two methods, and d > 0 means TrajPE is better. For the lower-is-better metrics (all >= 0) it equals the bench-v1.1 d; for higher-is-better metrics (Kendall tau, F1, NDCG, next-POI acc@k/ndcg@k/mrr) it replaces the v1.1 loss 1 - v, which shrank differences between small values (e.g. MRR 0.08 vs 0.07: v1.1 d = 0.005, bench-v1.2.1 d = 0.067). The absolute values in the denominator keep d in [-1, 1] with the sign of the improvement when a Kendall tau is negative
statistics.family_score: D = unweighted mean of d (metric_difference above) over the family's primary metrics that both methods have in that dataset x eps (restricted to the metric subset of the summary, e.g. unmeasured only); a family cell with no such metric is absent
statistics.family_counts: win if D > 0, loss if D < 0, tie if |D| <= 1e-12 (on the seed-0 values; no per-cell test)
statistics.headline: per baseline over all family cells both methods have: W/T/L, median D, Wilcoxon signed-rank test on D (two-sided, zeros dropped; primary test) and sign test (two-sided binomial; secondary), each Holm-corrected over baselines. TrajPE beats a baseline on the headline iff Holm-Wilcoxon p < 0.05 and the median of the non-tied D (the values the test uses) is > 0; loses iff p < 0.05 and that median is < 0; otherwise no significant difference (n.s., with the sign of the win/loss majority)
statistics.ranks: per family cell and method: mean of the method's per-metric ranks (by loss, ties averaged) over the family's metrics that every compared method has, re-ranked within the family cell (ties averaged); average over the family cells where every method is present; Friedman test and Nemenyi CD with N = number of such family cells
statistics.per_paper: per baseline and paper suite: the suite's primary metrics are grouped into the families above (restricted to the suite), giving family cells (dataset, eps, family); W/T/L and median D over them, Wilcoxon (primary) and sign test, Holm over the 8 suites within each baseline; also the paper-cell score (mean of the suite's family D per dataset x eps) with its W/T/L. Verdict: as the headline, on the suite's family cells: 'win' iff Holm-Wilcoxon p < 0.05 and the median of the non-tied D > 0, 'loss' iff p < 0.05 and it is < 0, otherwise 'n.s.' with the sign of the family-cell win/loss majority
statistics.v3_split: the family summaries are repeated for the near + unmeasured, unmeasured-only and measured subsets of bench-v1.1 (Section 6): the metric subset is applied first, then families are formed from the remaining metrics
statistics.outputs: with scripts/bench_tables.py --families configs/benchmark_protocol_v1.2.1_families.json --seeds 0: tables_families.md (which starts with the v1.1 metric-level headline), family_cells.csv and summary_families.json (with 'metric_level_v1_1') next to the unchanged v1.1 outputs; without --families the output is byte-identical to bench-v1.1, and with the bench-v1.2 file to bench-v1.2
statistics.seeds: owner rule 2026-10-22: every method is run with seed 0 only, so each method has ONE release per dataset x eps. The headline and per-paper verdicts use the seed-0 releases of every method (bench_tables.py --seeds 0), also for methods that have further finished seeds; those may be reported in a separate, labeled table (all seeds, seed means) and are never mixed into the headline
statistics.per_cell: no per-cell test: with one release per method the v1.1 per-cell Welch t-test is untestable in every cell (bench_tables.py reports such cells as 'untestable' and counts them by value only); a cell is a win/tie/loss by its value. Release-to-release (seed) variance is not estimated separately; it is part of the variation of the paired differences across cells
statistics.inference: paired tests across cells: for each baseline, the family scores D of the (dataset, eps, family) cells both methods have are the paired observations (Wilcoxon signed-rank, primary; sign test, secondary; Holm over baselines); per paper the same over the suite's family cells with Holm over the 8 suites within a baseline; the v1.1 metric level uses the d of the (dataset, eps, metric) cells in the same way. The unit of replication is the dataset x eps (x family) cell, so the tests speak about the population of cells for the given releases

reporting: every report of the benchmark (paper, go/no-go) gives, with equal prominence and side by side: the bench-v1.2.1 family-level headline per baseline, the bench-v1.1 metric-level headline per baseline (W/T/L of the primary metric cells, Wilcoxon/sign, Holm), and the per-paper verdicts. A method is called better than a baseline only where the family headline says so; where the metric-level headline disagrees, the disagreement is stated

v3_split_descriptors.rule: feature descriptors of workload families that bench-v1.1 (configs/benchmark_protocol_v1.json v3_split) does not describe, written from the family definitions in trajpe/workload.py only, in the variable vocabulary of the metric features (length class -> length, travel distance -> travel, diameter -> diameter, (first, last) cell -> first_cell/last_cell, cell transitions -> cell_pair, 3-hour block of the week -> time_of_week). Resolution, conditioning on the length class and per-trail weighting are ignored, as in bench-v1.1 Section 6; the measured/near/unmeasured labels then follow from the unchanged rule of bench_metrics.classify. bench_tables.py adds them when this file is passed with --families and refuses one that redefines a family the protocol already describes. The hybrid configs (configs/hybrid_*_eps.json) use the same workload families; the DP-SGD fine-tuned generator of the hybrid releases no histogram and adds no descriptor.

tdist.source: workload.py tdist: (length class 2|3|4|>=5) x travel distance (sum of hop lengths), per trail

diam.source: workload.py diam: one bin for L = 2, else (length class 3|4|>=5) x diameter, per trail

od6.source: workload.py od6: (first cell, last cell) on the public 6 x 6 grid, per trail (as od8)

ctrans6.source: workload.py ctrans6: cell -> cell transitions on the public 6 x 6 grid (as ctrans8/16)

tcell6.source: workload.py tcell6: (3-hour block of the week) x (cell of the public 6 x 6 grid), per check-in
